props.gloss_en: Rava b. Rav Ilai: 'because the daughters of Zion are haughty' (Isa 3:16) -- they would walk with upright stature
'and walk with outstretched necks' -- they would walk heel beside toe
'and wanton eyes' -- they would fill their eyes with kohl and beckon
'walking and mincing as they go' -- they would walk a tall one beside a short one

Rav Yitzchak of the school of R' Ami: 'and tinkling with their feet' teaches that they put myrrh and balsam in their shoes and walked in the markets of Jerusalem, and on reaching the young men of Israel kicked the ground, splashed it on them and put the evil inclination into them like a viper's venom
the Gemara: what was their punishment?
the Gemara's answer: their punishment is what Isa 3:24 describes, as Rabba bar Ulla expounded it
Rabba bar Ulla: 'instead of a sweet smell there shall be a stench' (Isa 3:24) -- the place they perfumed became rotting sores
'and instead of a sash, a rope' -- the place where they were girded with a sash became covered with bruises
'and instead of well-set hair, baldness' -- the place where they adorned themselves became bald patches
'and instead of a fine dress, a girding of sackcloth' -- the openings that bring to pleasure [petach-gil] shall be for a girding of sackcloth
Rava: 'for instead of beauty, a brand' -- this is what people say: instead of beauty, a sore
R' Yosei b. R' Chanina: 'and the Lord will smite with a scab the crown of the daughters of Zion' (Isa 3:17) teaches that leprosy broke out among them
one [of Rav and Shmuel]: 'and the Lord will lay bare their pot'hen' -- they were poured out like a jug
the other: their openings became like a forest

Rav: the people of Jerusalem were people of arrogance -- a man would say to his fellow: on what did you dine today? on kneaded bread or unkneaded? on white wine or dark? on a wide couch or a narrow one? with a good companion or a bad one?
Rav Chisda: and all of them [refer] to promiscuity
R' Yehuda: the wood of Jerusalem was cinnamon, and when they burned it its fragrance spread through all of Eretz Yisrael
and since Jerusalem was destroyed they were hidden away; only a barley-grain's worth remained, and it is found in the treasury of queen Tzimtzemai
